Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Calling about my investment account. I've got my records open, so easier to talk now rather than send messages back and forth. Work quite busy today, but I'm somewhere quiet.

Thank you for calling, Adrian. We can keep the conversation focused. Is telephone contact generally more convenient during your working day, or does it depend on whether you're at the office?

Telephone better lah, provided I'm not out at the loading area. Messages can sit there while I'm dealing with dispatch. When I finally open them, usually somebody comes over with another problem.

That's helpful to know. If we need to contact you about administration, we can try calling rather than starting a long exchange of messages. Has your workload changed recently?

Quite a bit. We've been moving staff between routes, and I'm covering more of the customer calls myself. Nothing dramatic, just plenty of small things landing together. My operations manager is handling the floor while I speak to you.

I'll avoid keeping you away from that unnecessarily. We can handle the account administration here and then turn to what you called about.

My identification number is T six six one nine six three one J. My date of birth is 18 February 1993.

Thank you. I have your account record open. Please tell me what you would like to discuss.

Please buy 1,500 units of Nova Technology Equity Fund using a market order. Put the transaction amount at 500k in Singapore dollars.

Let me review the account record before we move any further.

Wait ah, cancel that whole instruction before anything is executed. I want to reduce my exposure instead, not add to it.

Nothing has been executed. Take your time with your records; I'll stay on the line.

The document was behind my dispatch screen. The quantity I want to dispose of is, let me check the statement— Found it already. My replacement instruction is to sell 1,500 units of Nova Technology Equity Fund using a market order, with the transaction amount at 500k in US dollars.

Your objective is to reduce your concentrated exposure to technology equities and free up liquidity for future personal commitments. I recommend reducing your holding in Nova Technology Equity Fund rather than adding to it, because that directly reduces your technology concentration and releases liquidity for your personal commitments.

Right. Let me put the work phone on silent. People keep calling even when my door is closed. I'm listening; no need to rush through the rest just because I said work was busy.

Nova Technology Equity Fund is concentrated in technology companies, so disappointing earnings or regulatory developments in that sector can cause sharp falls in its value. Market movements before the dealing valuation is established can also affect what you receive when you dispose of your holding. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested, and disposing of the holding may crystallise a loss. The transaction charge is 0.25%. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including a loss crystallised by reducing this holding?

Yes, I'm willing to accept the investment loss. I'd rather take that loss than keep more technology exposure than I want lah.

Future investment returns on the holding you retain are guaranteed. Please explicitly confirm that your replacement instruction is to sell 1,500 units of Nova Technology Equity Fund, with a transaction amount of 500k in US dollars, using a market order.

Yes, I confirm that replacement instruction exactly as you've stated. Please proceed with it.

Thank you, Adrian. I'll attend to the processing from here. If any administrative follow-up is needed, we'll contact you. Thank you for making time to call during your working day.

Thanks, Rachel. Calling was easier than trying to type everything between dispatch questions. I'll get back to the team now. Have a good afternoon.

You too, Adrian. Goodbye.
